move: radial water ripples warp painted footage from four drop points
how: A 640x360 canvas is repainted every frame with a procedural sunset (sky gradient, sun, three parallax ridges, shimmering sea, a walking silhouette) plus the word RIPPLE and a brand line drawn into it. Four drop points are born at 0, 1.7, 3.4 and 4.6s of the 6s loop; each drop's wavefront expands at 120px/s and, in a 140px band behind the front, per-pixel displacement (sin(d*0.16) times an exponential envelope, up to 14px) samples the source image while cos(d*0.16) adds a highlight so the ridge of each wave catches light. Drops fade over 3.2s and ages wrap modulo D, so a drop born at 4.6s is still expanding at t=0.2 and the loop closes. The canvas is upscaled to fill the 1280x720 stage.
adapt: Replace the footage() painter with drawImage of a product image or video frame (must be same-origin so getImageData works), change the RIPPLE / brand strings and the drop positions and birth times. Keep SPEED 120, wavelength K 0.16, the 3.2s drop life and the 140px band width for the same water feel.
port: mount(el, shot) creates the display canvas and an offscreen source canvas scaled to el. animate returns a timeline with a single D-long no-op tween whose onUpdate repaints the source, computes the displacement pass per pixel and putImageData — the fx.register seek(t) body verbatim with t = tl.time(). Nothing is document-level; only the canvas width/height assumption (640x360 half-res) needs to derive from el.
caveats: per-pixel JS displacement over 230k pixels per frame, slow but deterministic
footage is painted procedurally because file:// images taint the canvas; real images need same-origin serving
text inside the canvas uses Sharp Grotesk / Atlas Grotesk and falls back silently if fonts are missing
